title: Luxury Villas for Sale in Phuket: What ฿20 Million and More Buys
excerpt: 53 of the 143 villas we list for sale cost ฿20 million or more, at a median of ฿26 million. Almost all are in Bang Tao or Rawai. What the top of the market looks like, and what to check.
author: Islander Home Team
content:
At the higher end of the Phuket property market, the priorities change. The question is no longer whether you can have a pool, but how large the plot is, what the view looks like, and how close the property is to Laguna or Nai Harn beach.

As of early November 2026 we list 143 villas for sale, at a median of ฿17.9 million. 53 of them cost ฿20 million or more. The figures below cover those 53 properties.

The numbers

  • Median price: ฿26 million
  • Bedrooms: mostly three (21) or four (22); eight have five
  • Typical plot: about 490 sq.m
  • Typical living area: about 400 sq.m

Bang Tao and Rawai dominate the luxury villa market. Forty-six of the 53 properties are in these two areas. Bang Tao villas are close to Laguna, Boat Avenue and the west-coast beaches, while Rawai villas are concentrated around Nai Harn, Saiyuan and the hills above the south coast. The median price is almost identical in both areas.

A few examples from the current list

  • A three-bedroom sea-view pool villa 80 m from the sea, Ao Po: ฿20 million
  • A three-bedroom pool villa in Laguna: ฿20.8 million
  • A ready-to-move-in pool villa near Layan Beach: ฿22 million
  • A five-bedroom pool villa in Saiyuan, Rawai: ฿22.9 million
  • A four-bedroom gallery loft villa in Nai Harn: ฿36.9 million
  • A five-bedroom pool villa in Bang Tao: ฿53 million

The most expensive property on the list is a six-bedroom villa in Rawai on about 2,300 sq.m of land, priced at ฿120 million.

What to check at this price

  • How you will own it. Foreigners cannot own land in their own name, so a villa is usually purchased through a registered lease or a structure approved by your lawyer. At this price level, seek legal advice before proceeding.
  • The land title. Check the title type and exact plot boundaries, particularly for hillside properties.
  • Rental history. If you plan to rent out the villa, ask for actual booking records and income figures rather than projections.
  • Running costs. Maintaining a large villa can involve significant costs for the pool, garden, staff, electricity and insurance. Ask the seller for last year's bills.

This is general information, not legal advice. Have a licensed Thai lawyer review the title and contract before signing.
